# Overview

This page derives the semi-classical framework governing the interaction between a laser field and a two-level atom. The results — Rabi oscillations, the full Optical Bloch Equations (OBEs), and the steady-state saturation formula — underpin every aspect of Rydberg atom control, from single-qubit gates to fluorescence imaging.

---

# Two-Level Atom in a Classical Field

## Hamiltonian and Dipole Approximation

In the dipole approximation ($k \to 0$, i.e., the field is spatially uniform over the atom), a two-level atom $\{|g\rangle, |e\rangle\}$ interacting with a monochromatic field $E = E_0 \cos(\omega t)$ polarized along $z$ has Hamiltonian

$$
H = \begin{pmatrix} E_g & \hbar\Omega\cos\omega t \\ \hbar\Omega\cos\omega t & E_e \end{pmatrix},
$$ {#eq-H-full}

where the **Rabi frequency** $\Omega = \langle g|eE_0 z|e\rangle / \hbar$ is real (absorbed into a phase of $|e\rangle$). The Rabi frequency for a Gaussian beam of power $P$ and waist $w_0$ driving the transition $(n,l,j,m_j) \to (n',l',j',m_j')$ is

$$
\Omega = \sqrt{\frac{4P}{\varepsilon_0 c \pi w_0^2}}\,\frac{\langle nljm_j | r_q | n'l'j'm_j'\rangle}{\hbar}.
$$ {#eq-rabi-gaussian}

## Rotating-Wave Approximation

The Schrödinger equation for @eq-H-full is

$$
i\hbar\begin{pmatrix}\dot c_1 \\ \dot c_2\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} E_g & \hbar\Omega\cos\omega t \\ \hbar\Omega\cos\omega t & E_e\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Define rotating-frame amplitudes $c_1 = \tilde c_1$, $c_2 = \tilde c_2 e^{-i\omega t}$. Substituting and using $\dot c_2 = (\dot{\tilde c}_2 - i\omega\tilde c_2)e^{-i\omega t}$:

$$
i\hbar\begin{pmatrix}\dot{\tilde c}_1 \\ \dot{\tilde c}_2\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & \hbar\Omega\cos\omega t\;e^{-i\omega t} \\ \hbar\Omega\cos\omega t\;e^{i\omega t} & E_e - \hbar\omega\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\tilde c_1 \\ \tilde c_2 \end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-rotating-frame}

Expanding $\cos\omega t\;e^{\pm i\omega t} = \frac{1}{2}(1 + e^{\pm 2i\omega t})$, we identify the rapidly oscillating $e^{\pm 2i\omega t}$ terms. Discarding them (the **rotating-wave approximation**) gives the time-independent Hamiltonian in the rotating frame:

$$
H_S/\hbar = \frac{\Omega}{2}(\sigma_- + \sigma_+) + \frac{\delta}{2}(\mathbb{I} + \sigma_z),
$$ {#eq-H-RWA}

where $\delta = (E_e - E_g)/\hbar - \omega$ is the laser detuning (atom minus laser; $\delta > 0$ for red-detuned light). The neglected counter-rotating terms produce the **Bloch–Siegert shift** $\sim \Omega^2/(4\omega)$, negligible for optical transitions.

## Rabi Oscillations

Integrating @eq-H-RWA from $|g\rangle$ at $t = 0$ yields the excited-state population:

$$
P_e(t) = \frac{\Omega^2}{\Omega^2 + \delta^2}\,\sin^2\!\left(\frac{t}{2}\sqrt{\Omega^2 + \delta^2}\right).
$$ {#eq-rabi-prob}

The **generalized Rabi frequency** $\tilde\Omega = \sqrt{\Omega^2 + \delta^2}$ sets the oscillation rate. The amplitude is reduced by $\Omega^2/\tilde\Omega^2$ for non-zero detuning; on resonance ($\delta = 0$), the atom oscillates between $|g\rangle$ and $|e\rangle$ with unit contrast.

**AC Stark shift.** The dressed-state eigenvalues are $E_\pm = (\delta \pm \tilde\Omega)/2$. In the far-detuned limit $\Omega \ll |\delta|$,

$$
E_+ - E_- \approx |\delta| + \frac{\Omega^2}{2|\delta|},
$$

so the ground state is shifted by $-\Omega^2/(4\delta)$ (downward for red-detuned light, $\delta > 0$), which is the attractive light shift exploited in optical tweezers trapping.

---

# Density Matrix Formalism Without Decay

For a mixed-state or open-system treatment, work with the density matrix $\rho$. Setting $E_g = 0$, $E_e = \hbar\omega_e$, the von Neumann equation $i\hbar\dot\rho = [H, \rho]$ gives

$$
i\begin{pmatrix}\dot\rho_{gg} & \dot\rho_{ge} \\ \dot\rho_{eg} & \dot\rho_{ee}\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}
(\rho_{eg} - \rho_{ge})\Omega\cos\omega t & (\rho_{ee} - \rho_{gg})\Omega\cos\omega t - \rho_{ge}\omega_e \\
(\rho_{gg} - \rho_{ee})\Omega\cos\omega t + \rho_{eg}\omega_e & (\rho_{ge} - \rho_{eg})\Omega\cos\omega t
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-vonNeumann-explicit}

Applying the rotating-frame substitution $\tilde\rho_{gg} = \rho_{gg}$, $\tilde\rho_{ee} = \rho_{ee}$, $\tilde\rho_{ge} = \rho_{ge}e^{-i\omega t}$, $\tilde\rho_{eg} = \rho_{eg}e^{i\omega t}$, and eliminating $e^{\pm 2i\omega t}$ terms, the equation becomes the **undamped Bloch equations**:

$$
\begin{pmatrix} \dot{\tilde\rho}_{gg} & \dot{\tilde\rho}_{ge} \\ \dot{\tilde\rho}_{eg} & \dot{\tilde\rho}_{ee} \end{pmatrix}
= -i\begin{pmatrix}
(\tilde\rho_{eg} - \tilde\rho_{ge})\frac{\Omega}{2} & (\tilde\rho_{ee} - \tilde\rho_{gg})\frac{\Omega}{2} - \tilde\rho_{ge}\delta \\
(\tilde\rho_{gg} - \tilde\rho_{ee})\frac{\Omega}{2} + \tilde\rho_{eg}\delta & (\tilde\rho_{ge} - \tilde\rho_{eg})\frac{\Omega}{2}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-bloch-nodamp}

---

# Spontaneous Emission

## Master Equation for Decay

Coupling to the radiation bath (vacuum or thermal) in free space drives the atom according to the Lindblad master equation. For the relevant Rydberg transitions, the decay rate is [@steck_optic_atoms]

$$
\Gamma = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{4\omega_0^3 \,|\langle g|e\vec r|e\rangle|^2}{3\hbar c^3}.
$$ {#eq-decay-rate}

At temperature $T$, the thermal photon occupation at frequency $\omega_0$ is $\bar n_{k_0} = (e^{\hbar\omega_0/k_BT} - 1)^{-1}$. The full master equation reads [@Quantumoptics]:

$$
\dot\rho_a = -\frac{\Gamma}{2}(\bar n + 1)\bigl[\sigma_+\sigma_-\rho_a - \sigma_-\rho_a\sigma_+\bigr]
            - \frac{\Gamma}{2}\bar n\bigl[\rho_a\sigma_-\sigma_+ - \sigma_+\rho_a\sigma_-\bigr] + \text{h.c.}
$$ {#eq-master-decay}

## Coherent-State Equivalence

To combine decay with coherent driving, one must justify replacing the quantized field by a classical time-dependent term. The rigorous Hamiltonian for a fixed atom in an electromagnetic field is

$$
H = \frac{(p - eA(r))^2}{2M} + V_c + H_R,
$$

where $H_R$ is the free-field Hamiltonian. We treat the laser as a coherent state evolving under $H_R$:

$$
|\alpha(t)\rangle = T(t)|0\rangle = \prod_i e^{\alpha a_i^\dagger(t) - \alpha^* a_i(t)}|0\rangle.
$$

Moving to the displaced frame $\psi' = T(t)\psi$ transforms the Schrödinger equation:

$$
\frac{d\psi'}{dt} = \left(\frac{dT}{dt}T^\dagger + THT^\dagger\right)\psi' = H'\psi'.
$$

A direct calculation shows that the displaced Hamiltonian is

$$
H' = \frac{(p - eA(r) - eA_e(\alpha_i, r, t))^2}{2M} + V_c + H_R,
$$

which corresponds to the substitution $A \to A + A_e$. Under the dipole approximation, this gives

$$
H_{SR} = H_S + H_R + eE(0,0)\cdot r + eE_e(0,\alpha,t)\cdot r,
$$

where the additional classical term $eE_e$ acts as the coherent drive. In this displaced frame, the photon field remains in the vacuum state, so the spontaneous emission rate $\Gamma$ is identical to the free-space rate [@Quantumoptics]. Therefore, one may simply superpose the classical Rabi drive and the Lindblad decay terms.

---

# Full Optical Bloch Equations

Combining the coherent Rabi drive (@eq-bloch-nodamp) with the spontaneous emission term from @eq-master-decay, with $\gamma = \Gamma/2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{\tilde\rho}_{gg} &= -i(\tilde\rho_{eg} - \tilde\rho_{ge})\frac{\Omega}{2} + 2\gamma\tilde\rho_{ee}, \\
\dot{\tilde\rho}_{ee} &= -i(\tilde\rho_{ge} - \tilde\rho_{eg})\frac{\Omega}{2} - 2\gamma\tilde\rho_{ee}, \\
\dot{\tilde\rho}_{ge} &= -i(\tilde\rho_{ee} - \tilde\rho_{gg})\frac{\Omega}{2} + i\tilde\rho_{ge}\delta - \gamma\tilde\rho_{ge}, \\
\dot{\tilde\rho}_{eg} &= -i(\tilde\rho_{gg} - \tilde\rho_{ee})\frac{\Omega}{2} - i\tilde\rho_{eg}\delta - \gamma\tilde\rho_{eg}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-OBE-full}

## Steady State

Setting all time derivatives to zero in @eq-OBE-full and solving:

$$
\rho_{ee}^{\rm ss} = \frac{s_0/2}{1 + s_0 + (2\delta/\Gamma)^2}, \qquad s_0 = \frac{I}{I_{\rm sat}} = \frac{2\Omega^2}{\Gamma^2}.
$$ {#eq-ss-pop}

:::{.callout-note icon="false"}
## Definition: Saturation parameter

The **saturation parameter** $s_0 = 2\Omega^2/\Gamma^2 = I/I_{\rm sat}$ measures the ratio of coherent driving to spontaneous emission. Above saturation ($s_0 \gg 1$), the population saturates at $\rho_{ee} \to 1/2$ regardless of $\delta$; the photon scattering rate saturates at $\Gamma/2$. The saturation intensity is $I_{\rm sat} = \hbar\omega_0^3\Gamma/(12\pi c^2)$.
:::

The on-resonance scattering rate $R_{\rm sc} = \Gamma\rho_{ee}^{\rm ss}|_{\delta=0} = \Gamma s_0/(2 + 2s_0)$ controls the fluorescence signal in imaging (see [Trapping and Cooling](trapping_cooling.qmd)) and the Doppler cooling force.

---

# Quantized Field and Jaynes-Cummings Picture

For the connection to Rydberg excitation physics, it is useful to state the fully quantized version. The interaction-picture Hamiltonian for a two-level atom coupled to a single mode of frequency $\omega$ near resonance is

$$
H_{SR,I} = \hbar g\bigl[a^\dagger\sigma_- e^{-i\delta t} + a\sigma_+ e^{i\delta t}\bigr],
$$ {#eq-JC}

where $g$ is the single-photon coupling strength. For a coherent state with large mean photon number $\bar n \gg 1$, tracing over the field recovers the classical Rabi result with $\Omega = 2\sqrt{\bar n}\,g$ [@steck_optic_atoms]. The interaction-picture atom Hamiltonian becomes

$$
H_{S,I}/\hbar = \frac{\Omega}{2}\bigl(\sigma_- e^{-i\delta t} + \sigma_+ e^{i\delta t}\bigr).
$$ {#eq-H-interaction}

This is the starting point for the two-qubit gate analysis in [Two-Qubit Gates](two_qubit_gates.qmd).
